findings.title: `fire_unit_until` blocks until the unit ends, so the early stop never runs
findings.description:
`fire_unit_until` calls `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)` and only then calls `wait_for_unit_or_line`. `run` wraps a blocking `subprocess.run`. `deploy/mt-run` `start_and_stream` (lines 127-143) starts the unit and loops `while is_running "${unit}"; do sleep 2; done`. So `mt-run minute` returns only after the pass has ended. By the time the journal-line polling starts, the unit is already gone, and `reached and unit_active(unit)` is never true. The ten-hour firing that issue #22 set out to fix is unchanged.

The new tests patch `cutover_common.run` and `unit_active`, so they can't see this. The function needs to start the unit without waiting. Options are `systemctl start --no-block` through the sudoers-listed commands, or running `mt-run` under `Popen` and polling while it runs. The tests should then model a blocking `mt-run`.

findings.title: Sudoers rule is effectively full root, and its header says otherwise
findings.description:
The header says "Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider". The rule is wider than that.
- `MT_INSTALL` names a script inside the operator's own checkout (`/home/manta/.../deploy/install-production.sh`). The `manta` user can edit that file and then run it as root with no password.
- `MT_RUN = /usr/local/bin/mt-run *` accepts any arguments. `mt-run` falls through to `run_production_mt "$@"` (`deploy/mt-run:197`). That runs the production `mt` CLI with the service credentials from `/etc/manta-trading.env`, as `manta-trading` or root.
- The `systemctl ... mt-*` wildcards match any trailing arguments.

If this is an accepted trade-off for a single trusted operator, say so in the header instead of claiming a narrow grant. Otherwise install the script root-owned and not user-writable, and restrict the `mt-run` and `mt-*` arguments. The `MT_READ` grant for `cat /etc/manta-trading.env` is inherent to `cutover_common.py:226`, but it exposes all secrets in that file and should be called out.

findings.title: Cagg-freshness probe probably matches nothing, so verify may wait forever
findings.description:
The job lookup filters `job.hypertable_name = %s` with the cagg view name (`minute_4hour_ohlcv`). In TimescaleDB, `timescaledb_information.jobs.hypertable_name` for a continuous-aggregate refresh policy normally holds the internal materialization hypertable (`_materialized_hypertable_N`), not the view name. I couldn't check this against a live database. If it is true, `job_row` is `None`, `last_refresh` is `None`, and `CaggFreshness.stale` is `True` whenever any bar exists. `--verify` would then answer WAIT on every run.

A missing job row is also silently folded into "stale". That conflicts with the project rule against silent fallbacks, and it should raise or report that no refresh policy was found. The unit test (`test_the_probe_reads_the_job_stats_and_the_session_chunk`) uses a mock cursor and asserts only that the SQL text contains the proc name, so it can't catch a wrong join key. Run the query against a real TimescaleDB, or join through `continuous_aggregates.materialization_hypertable_name`.

findings.title: Import order is broken in several files, which fails the required `I` ruff rule
findings.description:
`pyproject.toml` selects `I`. Several import blocks are out of isort order.
- `minute.py`: `data.acquisition.daemon.minute_sessions` sits after `data.gaps`, with a stray blank line splitting the first-party block. `data.gaps.repair_921` also comes before `data.gaps.minute_coverage`.
- `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:45-52`: `NOTES_DIR, fire_unit_until, start_log, CutoverError, ...` is not sorted. The `# noqa: E402` comment doesn't cover I001.
- `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py:60`: `cagg_freshness_for_session` comes before `CheckReport`.
- `test/unit/test_repair_921.py:30`: `CaggFreshness, cagg_freshness_for_session, SymbolFindings, ...` is out of order.

Run `ruff check --fix`.

findings.title: The `"[WAIT]"` sentinel is a bare string repeated across modules
findings.description: `repair_921_minute_sessions.py` prints a literal `"[WAIT]"`. The cutover script then does substring matches on `"[WAIT]"` and `"FAIL"` in four places (`_verify_when_fresh`, the loop condition, the `ok` computation, and the tests). Changing the token would need edits in several files. The project rule is to define such a value once and reference it everywhere. Put the WAIT marker in one constant, or better, have `--verify` return a distinct exit code instead of text matching. Also, `_verify_when_fresh` runs twice in the happy path, so the final acceptance step can add up to another 75 minutes of polling.

findings.title: Production daemon now depends on a one-off repair module
findings.description: `minute.py` imports `RepairScanTimeout` and `build_truncated_day_index` from `data.gaps.repair_921`, which is named for a single slice's repair script. The recurring trailing walk now relies on it. Move the truncated-day index into a durable gaps module such as `minute_coverage`, and keep `repair_921` as a consumer of it.

findings.title: An extra pool connection and query for every minute chunk
findings.description:
Each chunk now opens a separate `pool.connection()` just to run `fetch_session_bounds`. The chunk loop already opens a connection for the write a few lines later. Across thousands of symbols with many chunks, that is an added round-trip per chunk. Reuse the per-chunk connection, or fetch the bounds once per symbol for the gap's range.

A related behavior change is worth confirming. A session the provider hasn't published now produces PARTIAL, which increments `attempt_count` and can promote the row to `RETRY_EXHAUSTED`. That is correct for the 01:05 case. A permanently empty session, such as a half day with no data, could also exhaust its retries. The tests don't cover that path.

findings.title: Narration log misses some operator output
findings.description: `say` is tee'd to the log file, but `print` calls in `fire_unit_until`, `wait_for_unit_or_line` and `fire_unit` are not. The "full narration" label overstates what the file holds. `test/unit/data/acquisition/daemon/test_minute.py` also repeats about 40 lines of mock scaffolding between `_run` and `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success`. A shared fixture in `conftest.py` would remove that.

findings.title: Session-judgement logic and timer/constant consistency
findings.description: `judge_chunk_by_sessions` is pure and uses the same `(open, close]` predicate as the repair index. The tests use real EODHD bar shapes and cover the spillover-only, weekend-tail and no-session edge cases. `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC`, `mt-minute-pass.timer`, the health-check docstrings and the tests all agree on 04:05. The UTC formatting fix in `minute_session_mass.py` is correct.
